sentences.text: 1 This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 22.05.2024 at about 10.00 p.m. petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ- 9214 near Manipal Hospital Signal Light Junction, Mysore City, at that time, driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-F-5054 drove the bus at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle, due to the forced impact, petitioner SCCH-5 fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent around Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance and other incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 40 years, hale and healthy, working as Security Guard at VST Company, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he is bed ridden,under treatment and not able to do any work and suffering from permanent disability.
With regard to accident crime No.59/2024 is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle before the Narasimharaja Traffic Police.
Respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the KSRTC is liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
SCCH-5 4.

On service of notice, respondent has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement and denied occurrence of the accident and involvement of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-09-F- 5054.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.05.2024 at about 10.00 p.m. near Manipal Hospital Signal light junction, Mysore City due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-09-F- 5054?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
SCCH-5 3. What order or award?

In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Medical Record Officer at Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital is examined as PW-2, further Dr.S.A.Somashekar,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-3 and marked 19 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.

On the other hand, driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-09-F-5054 is examined as RW-1.
7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:

Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2,
copy of mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.7.

During the cross examination of P.W-1 nothing is elicited to discard the evidence that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-F-5054.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Medical Record Officer and Doctor as PW-2 and PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and documents those have marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 22.05.2024 as alleged in the petition.
10. Per contra, driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-09-F-5054 is examined as RW-1.
R.W-1 stated that due to over speed the petitioner lost control and dashed to KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-F-5054 hence petitioner is responsible for occurrence of accident.

Further it is stated that in order to get compensation false case is foisted against the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-F-5054.
The time and place of accident is admitted by R.W-1.

It is to be noted that Respondent not challenged the chargesheet filed against the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-F-5054.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 22.05.2024 at about 10.00 p.m. while he was riding hiss motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- SCCH-5 53-EQ-9214 near Manipal Hospital Signal Light Junction, Mysore City.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-09-F-5054.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left clavicle fracture, for which he took conservative treatment.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Narayana Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 22.05.2024 to 23.05.2024.
Further he has exhibited medical bills of Rs.27,410/-.
SCCH-5 13

. Further Medical Record Officer at Narayana Multispeciality Hospital is examined as PW-2 and furnished authorization letter as Ex.P.13, copy of police intimation as Ex.P.14, copy of MLC as Ex.P.15, case sheet as Ex.P.16 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.17.
14.
Further examined Dr.S.A.Somashekar, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-3.
To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical notes as Ex.P.18 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.19 and he has assessed total disability of left upper limb at 26% and whole body at 13%.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has not assessed functional disability of the petitioner and he has not gone through the case sheet of petitioner, but verified the discharge summary.
Further deposed that, clavicle fracture is not a severe injury, hence petitioner was treated conservatively.
Further deposed that, fractures are mal-united and with SCCH-5 difficulty mal-union of fracture can be treated.
PW-3 deposed that, as per the guidelines after completion of treatment, disability has to be assessed.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 7%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 40 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 23.04.1984 and the alleged accident is occurred on 22.05.2024, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 his age is considered about 40 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

. As per his case, he was working as Security Guard at VST Company, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.16,500/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 22.05.2024 to 23.05.2024.

As per the SCCH-5 evidence of PW-3 he examined petitioner on 19.04.2025 i.e., after 11 months and on examination date as per version of PW-3 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least two months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.16,500/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.33,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.9 medical bill for Rs.27,410/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated SCCH-5 that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 22.05.2024.
So as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained clavicle fracture which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Yogesha for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW- 3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
19.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 2,07,900-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges
4. Medical Expenses 27,410-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 SCCH-5 6. Loss of income during laid up 33,000-00 period Total 3,23,310-00 20.

Accordingly this Tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,23,310/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent being the R.C Owner and internal insurer of the KSRTC is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the Sadhanandha C vs K.S.R.T.C on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32501391/
5 date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

22. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH-5 The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,23,310/- (Rupees three lakh twenty three thousand three hundred and ten only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

2025) (SHARMILA KAMATH K.)
